absent: Locking and concurrency rules for concurrent page table walks versus updates during diagnostics.
Full layout and width of page table entry flag fields and leaf detection semantics beyond presence and permission checks shown.
Complete set of error code bit definitions and trap number values.
Implementation of fixup, prefetch detection, stack guard info, firmware graceful handling, memory checker and arena handlers referenced but not routed.

findings.text: Page table diagnostic starts from current top level base and descends through four successive levels toward leaf. Before touching each level it probes readability with a fault suppressing helper and aborts to a short bad report if unreadable. At each present check it emits the raw entry value and stops early when an entry is absent or represents a large mapping, otherwise continues to finest granularity and terminates report with newline.

AMD specific workaround applies only on sixty four bit builds with AMD vendor support for a particular legacy family, in supervisor context, when fault address matches instruction pointer with cleared upper half. It canonicalizes address by setting upper bits and accepts only when result lies in kernel text bounds or module range, logging a one time warning and rewriting instruction pointer to canonical form to indicate handled.

Compatibility mode check reports true on sixty four bit builds when code segment indicates thirty two bit or user requested privilege context and fault address carries nonzero upper half, otherwise false.

Invalid lock workaround is active only when build enables the historic bug option and running CPU advertises the defect, for supervisor faults whose address falls in reserved descriptor table range. In that case it delegates to invalid opcode handling and reports handled, otherwise reports not handled.

Descriptor reporter derives table offset from selector index shifted by privilege width scaled by descriptor size. It rejects null selector, rejects offset plus long descriptor size beyond table limit, and rejects unreadable table slot, each with distinct alert. On success it assembles base from low middle and high portions with additional high portion on sixty four bit, and assembles limit from low and high portions for display with selector value.

Fault oops printer suppresses output when oops printing is disallowed. For instruction fetch faults it consults current mappings to distinguish execution of non executable present page and user page execution under supervisor execution protection, emitting critical hints with caller identity. It then distinguishes null dereference from generic fault, decodes user versus supervisor and fetch versus write versus read, decodes protection cause among not present reserved protection keys RMP and permissions, dumps descriptor tables and task register state for supervisor error observed in user mode, dumps page tables, and additionally dumps RMP state for RMP faults.

Global helper exposes host virtual to RMP diagnostic. It locates current top level, translates given address to leaf mapping and protection level, reports when no mapping exists, otherwise combines frame base with intra level offset to obtain physical address and forwards resulting frame number to RMP dump routine.

RMP dump first performs authoritative lookup. When entry is assigned it fetches raw contents and reports single frame with low and high raw words, handling lookup or fetch failures with error logs. When unassigned it scans the aligned large region containing the frame and reports only nonzero raw pairs, logging read errors per frame while continuing scan.

Raw RMP accessor requires initialized segment table and converts frame number to byte address. It derives segment table index and intra segment index through helpers, validates each against stored maxima with speculation hardening, rejects missing table null descriptor or out of range with distinct encoded errors, and otherwise returns pointer to indexed raw entry.
Segment index is defined as address shifted right by configurable segment shift. Entry index is defined as frame number of address masked by configurable segment mask.

Authoritative RMP lookup requires host secure nested paging capability, reads fine granularity entry for frame, then reads aligned large granularity entry to determine authoritative protection level, propagating any failure and reporting level through output parameter.

RMP read prefers hardware accelerated read when CPU feature is present, invoking it with frame address and output buffer and returning hardware status. Without acceleration it fetches raw entry, propagates encoded errors, clears output structure, and copies translated guest address plus ownership and attribute fields while leaving large region status unset.

Raw RMP entry exposes paired low and high words including guest frame ownership and attribute bits. Cooked form exposes translated guest address plus ownership assigned size and immutability fields with large region status intentionally omitted.

Corrupted table handler announces faulting task name and address, dumps page table state, enters oops context, invokes die routine with bad table label and fault context, suppresses signal when die reports handled, and closes oops context with kill signal otherwise.
Error sanitizer forces protection bit for fault addresses at or above maximum user task size to avoid disclosing kernel table layout through fault type, leaving lower addresses unchanged.
Signal context recorder stores page fault trap number and fault error code with user flag forced, plus fault address as saved control register value, into thread state of current task.

Kernel fault oops path first bypasses stack firmware and special device checks for implicit kernel access from user mode. It detects vmalloc stack guard overflow and switches to double fault stack to handle overflow, consults firmware graceful crash path when enabled, and allows memory checker and arena handlers to claim not present faults. Unclaimed faults enter oops context, print detailed fault report, warn on stack corruption, invoke die with oops label, emit executive fault address summary, and close oops context with kill signal unless handled.
Kernel mode dispatcher asserts supervisor context, returns when exception fixup claims fault, returns when prefetch erratum filter claims fault, otherwise forwards to kernel oops printer.

Segmentation notice is skipped when task handles fatal signal locally and when message rate limiting denies output. Otherwise it logs severity based on process identity with task name identifier fault address instruction pointer stack pointer error code and virtual memory location, appends likely processor and topology details, and dumps instruction bytes.

No semaphore bad area dispatcher routes supervisor register context to kernel fixup path and implicit user access to kernel memory to kernel oops path. For genuine user faults it enables interrupts, ignores prefetch and compatibility erratum cases, sanitizes error code, tries virtual system object fixup, optionally logs unhandled signal, records architecture signal context, and forces either protection key error with supplied key or generic segmentation fault with supplied code.
Thin wrapper supplies zero protection key and mapping error code to generic no semaphore handler.

Bad area release rule requires caller to hold either address space read lock or virtual area read lock. Handler releases address space lock when address space is present, otherwise ends virtual area read section, then delegates to no semaphore dispatcher without holding either.

Key based access test returns false when operating system key protection is disabled. When enabled it returns true if fault signals key violation or when architecture permission check denies write or execute access for current non foreign context, otherwise false.

Access error router selects protection key path when key test indicates denial, capturing key identifier from virtual area and using key error code, otherwise uses generic access error with zero key. Observed key may race with concurrent key changes and need not match faulting entry.

Bus fault handler forwards supervisor context to kernel fixup path with bus code and default key. For user context it ignores prefetch, sanitizes error, tries virtual system object fixup, records signal context, then on hardware poison delivers machine check bus error with size derived from large versus small poison indication, otherwise delivers generic bus address error.
Permission consistency check rejects write error against non writable entry and instruction error against non executable entry, accepting otherwise.

Spurious fault filter accepts only exact write plus protection and fetch plus protection error patterns. It walks initial kernel tables from top level, requiring present at each stage and delegating large mappings to permission check, requiring present leaf and validating leaf permissions, then additionally validating containing middle level permissions with one time warning on mismatch and returning final verdict.
Global integer flag controls whether unhandled fault signals produce user visible notices and defaults to enabled.

Lazy translation cache flush after kernel protection changes can deliver spurious write or fetch faults that must be filtered by revalidating permissions against initial tables rather than treated as real faults.
User mode view of kernel addresses must sanitize error protection bit to prevent disclosure of kernel table layout through fault type distinction.
Unassigned frame may still be inaccessible due to assigned neighbours within same large region when accessed through large host mapping, requiring region scan for diagnosis.
Stack overflow handling must switch to reserved double fault stack because current stack space may be insufficient and proceeding in oops path risks losing console and stack trace.
